steps.note: States h=100, banks X_a,Y_a indexed by a in T^3, N=v^3, m=h^3, the three stages forward/inverse/forward giving (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a), and restoration of every scratch wire for arbitrary initial values (matches paper 653-783, Lemma lem:scalar-motifs). Reason: the body calls it 'the finite building block of the later tape procedures', notes m is 'the dimension of the label space used later', and the Where-this-fits box places it as the first move of the plan (network -> frames -> rank per edge -> s<Wm -> recurrence). Why scratch restoration matters (scratch rows carry real data and must also receive H<-H+D) is only made explicit later, on address-interchange.md.

array-frames.md gives the common frame D_v per gate, the commutation G(D_v g_1,...)=D_v G(g_1,...), the implemented operator D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, telescoping to endpoint frames, and 'an edge costs whatever applying D_v D_u^{-1} costs' (paper 793-843). Its section 'What the free frames are for' says the interior frames are free to make each edge cheap and links forward to subspace-labels.md and rank-recurrence.md; rank-recurrence.md repeats that 'the only recursive work is changing frame along each edge'.

Labels are nondegenerate subspaces of F (x) F (x) F of dimension h^3=m; bit labels over Q^h with form I-J/9, complex labels over F_2^h with the dot product (matches paper 856-870). The [G|E] notation reproduces the paper's gate-label table (975-988): every arrow is an inclusion except centre 3->4, which drops P(x)F(x)Q of dimension h, and side 2->5 uses neighbour orthogonality (paper Lemma lem:motif-residuals, 997-1010). Reason: 'the labelling chooses the frames ... so that a network ... costs s<Wm smaller calls, the saving the recursion needs' and 'to save, the labels must confine all loss to one small edge'.

States that for nondegenerate U in U', Pi_{U'}-Pi_U projects onto U' cap U^perp with rank dim U'-dim U (same on reversed edge), so each edge's rank is its absolute dimension change, with the N first X_a edges as exceptions: zero dimension change but matrix 2 Pi_{U_a} of rank one (paper 1156-1166). Reason given just before: each projection matrix is a frame that adds it times one chunk to another, so an edge shears by the matrix difference and costs one smaller call per unit of rational rank; this is why rank, and hence dimension change, is the count of calls.

subspace-labels.md: source dimensions sum to N, sink dimensions to Wm-N, signed changes telescope at gates to Wm-2N, absolute changes Wm-2N+2L with L_b=I c_b h, plus N source ranks, so s_b=W_b m-(N-2L_b) (paper 891-897, 997-1010, 1138-1154). rank-recurrence.md ('Why s<Wm') gives the intuitive version: Wm would save nothing, bank wires save 2N, lost dimensions cost 2L, the sign at each X_a costs one rank. Reason: the budget is what makes s<Wm, which the recursion needs.

L_b/N=3c_b h/v=30000/161700=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539, both below 1/2 (paper 1105-1110); deficit N-2L_b=339/539 N>0 so s_b<W_b m (paper 1167), with the relative deficit 339/22587335000000 worked out from W_b=22587335/539 N (arithmetic checked). rank-recurrence.md explains why strictness is needed: with s=Wm the cost is proportional to Vf and nothing is saved.

subspace-labels.md: sources get -Pi_{U_a} at X_a and 0 elsewhere, and 'the negative source makes every route's endpoint difference Id, the same shear on every role: Pi_{U_a^perp}+Pi_{U_a} from X_a to Y_a, Pi_F-0 elsewhere' (paper 1169-1171). address-interchange.md states M_out(rho(w))-M_in(w)=I_m and derives f'_{rho(w)}=Phi_{I_m} f_w, i.e. H<-H+D on every original row including scratch rows (paper 1519-1533). Reason: address-interchange.md explains the interchange as D<-D-H, H<-H+D, D<-H-D with 'only the middle shear uses the circuit', so the identity is what lets the network perform the interchange.

matrix-shear.md gives A=E_1 Pi E_2 with E_1,E_2 invertible lower triangular and Pi with exactly a ones, triangular parts by controlled shifts in O(V), and each one of Pi done by one interchange, so exactly a interchanges plus O(V) (paper 1364-1447, including the prime q avoiding denominators). address-interchange.md: 'a shear by an edge matrix costs as many interchanges ... as its rank ... The number of recursive calls is the sum of the edge ranks, exactly s.' Reason: matrix-shear.md's Where-this-fits box says an edge of rank a costs a interchanges of fields of 1/m the width, feeding F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1); address-interchange.md: 'That change is a shear by A_i, which is why an edge costs its rank.'

address-interchange.md: W role streams of volume V/W, node work O(V), F_0=O(1), F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), geometric sum split at c<=1 and c>1, F_k=O(e^tau) with tau=1-2^{-50}, justified by eta>20*2^{-50} and log m<20 (paper 1319-1346, 1475-1557). rank-recurrence.md gives the same recurrence as C(mf)<=(s/W)C(f)+O(1), shows s=Wm would give no saving, and computes eta_b=339/22587335000000 and eta_c=73/19906842167500 (both match paper). Reason: the power saving is what makes the interchange cost O(Vu^tau), which the transform layout and cost accounting then use.

array-frames.md has an inline link in 'What the free frames are for': 'The later page Nested subspace labels and rank deficit makes this choice', plus the Connections and Used-by links.
Both on subspace-labels.md: the label table and the single decreasing edge, then the projection-rank argument a few paragraphs later.

Both on subspace-labels.md. The page states the budget Wm-2N+2L before the rank-equals-dimension argument and then combines them in the displayed s_b formula, so the order is reversed but the connection is explicit.
subspace-labels.md computes L/N=100/539 and 101/539 right after the budget and concludes s_b<W_b m; rank-recurrence.md (linked) restates both.

subspace-labels.md states the endpoint identity (route difference Id, the same shear on every role) right after the s_b<W_b m display. The fuller tape version (H<-H+D on every row, scratch included) is on address-interchange.md, which subspace-labels.md reaches only through rank-recurrence.md.

address-interchange.md states the endpoint contract M_out(rho(w))-M_in(w)=I_m and, in the next paragraphs, that each edge shear costs rank-many interchanges with s recursive calls in all. It links to matrix-shear.md for the E_1 Pi E_2 factorization.

address-interchange.md goes from 'the number of recursive calls is ... exactly s' to F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) and F_k=O(e^tau). matrix-shear.md also links to address-interchange.md in its Where-this-fits box, Connections and Used-by list.

summary: Yes: W1 carries a reader from the fixed exchange network to the exponent tau=1-2^{-50}. All nine steps appear with their defining content, each with a stated purpose, and nothing contradicts the paper (the numbers 100/539, 339/539, W_b=22587335/539 N, both eta values and the 20*2^{-50} margin all check). The chain only thins between subspace-labels.md, which holds C3-C7 and asserts 'one smaller call per unit of rank' without linking matrix-shear.md or address-interchange.md, and the tape side (C7-C9), which the reader reaches through rank-recurrence.md. The index's reading order also puts matrix-shear.md (C8) in Part 3, before the network it serves.
